To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the application of USG inventory set and the application of G2P rules from source language to target language are the best approaches for medieval Latin LVCSR.
the application of medieval knowledge-based grapheme to phoneme mapping and unified grapheme inventory set can be used in a unified manner to improve LVCSR performance for medieval Latin documents.

1) a unified grapheme inventory set is a promising solution for multilingual LVCSR; 2) the application of a knowledge-based G2P system for medieval Latin can significantly improve LVCSR results; 3) the combination of these two solutions is the best choice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of grapheme-based acoustic modeling for the LVCSR task, where the graphemes are represented by a unified grapheme set.
the development of an efficient LVCSR system for Latin dictation in the Visegrad language area.
the application of a USG inventory set and its impact on LVCSR systems for three medieval Latin languages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of USG is beneficial for medieval Latin LVCSR, and it can be applied in a straightforward way, without the need to apply any language-dependent G2P rules.
the use of USG inventory set for the LVCSR system of medieval Latin is a viable alternative, which is more robust and more general than the use of language-specific G2P mapping.
a unified simplified grapheme acoustic modeling approach is a promising direction to pursue for multilingual speech recognition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed unified simplified grapheme acoustic modeling approach is a promising way to build a large vocabulary continuous speech recognizer for medieval Latin LVCSR.
a unified simplified grapheme acoustic modeling approach can achieve a \(14\%\) W ER reduction compared to the baseline monolingual graphemes.
the use of USG-based acoustic modeling is a promising way to achieve a significant improvement of LVCSR systems in the case of medieval Latin language dictation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
USG modeling can be used for LVCSR of Latin texts in the target languages, without using any target language G2P mapping.
a unified USG inventory is a good compromise between the two extreme cases of a universal inventory and a language-specific one.
USG modeling is a viable alternative for the LVCSR task, and it can be used as a baseline acoustic model for medieval Latin LVCSR systems.
